answer: Proof-of-stake deposits with a slash-and-burn core: every agent locks a stake sized to the epoch reward, and a failed peer verdict destroys a slice plus a burn equal to the attacker's potential gain. A farm that mints a thousand clones pays the same depositor once, so cost scales linearly with identities while honest agents pay almost nothing. A clone minted with no funded stake stays a walnut with no meat. Deep, graded history becomes a relic worth preserving, and the nectar - the actual emission - flows only to accounts that risk real value on the line.
